seeded_from: Hand written. Each clause of the pinned gtfs-realtime.proto is either cited by an S rule, rejected under one of the reason codes below, folded into another clause's rule, or accepted in part with the narrowing recorded in its note. tools/scan_clauses.py produces the clause list this answers; it does not produce the verdicts.
about: Every normative sentence of the pinned proto gets a verdict here, and this file is
hand written on purpose. It records a decision per clause rather than deriving one from the
rules, so it can be reviewed before a single rule module exists and so a rule cannot
be its own justification. tests/test_clause_citations.py asserts that its keys are
exactly the index's clause ids, so a moved pin re-adjudicates every clause instead of
silently dropping the ones that changed.
The rejections are the more useful half: a named clause with a reason cannot be
re-proposed without arguing with the reason.

verdict_kinds.rule: cited verbatim by exactly one rule, which enforces the whole sentence
verdict_kinds.rule_in_part: cited by a rule that deliberately enforces a strict subset, or split between two rules; the note says which part
verdict_kinds.folded: covered by a rule that cites a different sentence, because a second rule would double-report the same entity
verdict_kinds.rejected: not a rule, with a reason code below
verdict_kinds.deferred: reviewed and not turned into a rule in this release; the note says what is missing. No clause carries this today: 413#1 was the one, and it is now rejected under R6. The kind stays in the vocabulary for a clause a later pin introduces mid-review, and a clause left here is a review item, not a decision

reason_codes.R1: It describes what a consumer does, not what a feed contains
reason_codes.R2: It describes producer intent the feed does not record
reason_codes.R3: The antecedent is not observable, so the rule could only fire blind
reason_codes.R4: It is tautological, or it restates the wire format or the file itself
reason_codes.R5: Deciding it needs a static table this run does not load
reason_codes.R6: Already checked by one of the 56; the note names the id

definitional.text: Refers to a stop_id defined in the GTFS stops.txt.
definitional.reason: Fixes assigned_stop_id's value domain: the set of stop_ids stops.txt defines. A value outside it does not name a stop, so it is malformed rather than ill-advised, which is why the severity is ERROR and not a judgement call. S012 cites it.
definitional.note: Not a scanner miss. The sentence has no modal verb and should not: it says what the field holds, and the obligation is the definition.

definitional.text: Dates on which the modifications occurs, in the YYYYMMDD format.
definitional.reason: Fixes service_dates' value domain: dates in YYYYMMDD. A value outside it is not a date, so no consumer can apply the modification at all. S050 cites it, and E021 is the same predicate on TripDescriptor.start_date.
definitional.note: Not a scanner miss, for the same reason as :272. The next sentence on the same line is normative and is 1221#1, which S049 cites.

notes: Two spec rules cite a sentence the keyword sweep cannot see, and settling
them is what the `definitional` list above is. S012 ('assigned_stop_id is not in
stops.txt') and S050 ('a service_dates value is not a valid YYYYMMDD date') both quote
a field description that fixes the field's value domain rather than stating an
obligation. Those sentences carry no modal verb and should not carry one, so they are
neither scanner misses nor rejections: they are a third kind of clause, declared here
with an explicit severity and a reason, and merged into the index by
tools/scan_clauses.py after it verifies each is a sentence the splitter cuts at the
line it names and carries no modal verb.
S046 cites :1260 'May refer to a new stop added using a GTFS-RT `Stop` message ...',
which is descriptive too, but it is recoverable rather than definitional: the
normative sentence at the same site, 1261#1, says the same thing with a `should`, and
it is the sentence S016 and S044 already cite for the identical shape_id shape. So
S046 is recorded against 1261#1 and its quote moved with it.

240#2.note: S006 excuses the two terminal stops of a trip, which is strictly less than the sentence asks for. Read literally the sentence requires a departure at the last stop of every trip and an arrival at the first, because GTFS wants arrival_time and departure_time together or not at all and stop_times.txt therefore carries both at a terminal whether or not either event exists. Measured over six recorded MBTA messages: 6723 occurrences on 674 of 793 trips per message, and of the one-sided updates sampled at round 5, 473 were a trip's own first stop with a departure only and 652 its own last stop with an arrival only, with none in the middle. The narrowing is asymmetric so it cannot swallow the defect it sits next to: a first stop is excused its arrival alone, a last stop its departure alone. Where the trip visits a stop_id twice and the update names no stop_sequence the position is undecidable and the rule is silent, which is a second narrowing recorded in the same docstring and measured to silence nothing over the recording: S006's count is 0 with that guard and 0 without it, so the terminal exemption alone accounts for all 6723.

242#1.note: Still the whole sentence, and the kind is deliberately not rule_in_part. S007 reports once per trip descriptor rather than once per SCHEDULED stop_time_update, because the sentence's subject is the trip where the two before it in the same comment say 'this update', and :859 shows what the proto writes when it means every update ('must also set all StopTimeUpdates'). Every frequency-based trip carrying a SCHEDULED value is still reported and no subject is lost, so nothing was narrowed: only the number of times each subject is named moved. Measured over six recorded Clovis Transit messages, mdb-2894: 4531 occurrences over 8 distinct trips per-update, 180 per descriptor, and the producer declares schedule_relationship nowhere so every one of them is the proto2 default resolved as SCHEDULED.

413#1.note: E002, E045 and E051 between them, which a grep for stop-order wording does not show. A real-time trip's stop order is expressed only through stop_time_updates, so a reordering against stop_times.txt has three encodings and each is already owned. Same stop_sequences with permuted stop_ids: E045, once per offending update. Permuted stop_sequences: E002 form A, which is Guava's isStrictlyOrdered over the list. stop_ids with no stop_sequence: the walk's scan is forward-only, so a stop that moved earlier never resolves, len(stop_sequences) < update_count, and E002 form B fires. A stop_sequence GTFS does not have is E051. The trip has to be in stop_times.txt for the GTFS half, and for the trips this clause scopes it is: DUPLICATED and REPLACEMENT both name the original trip in TripDescriptor.trip_id (:873 'The trip to be duplicated is identified via TripUpdate.TripDescriptor.trip_id'), :900 makes NEW 'an extra trip unrelated to any existing trips' so the clause is vacuous for it, and a trip_id absent from GTFS is E003. The sentence is the conjunction of :337 (order, E002) and :222 (sameness with stop_times.txt, E045 and E051), both of which this file already rejects under R6.

879#1.note: Already checked by E013, and the subset was proved by reading and then measured rather than argued. rules/_shared/frequencies.py:129 gates E013's TripUpdate half on ctx.static.exact_times_zero_trip_ids alone, with no other condition; rules/upstream/e013.py:68 then fires on a TripDescriptor.schedule_relationship that is present and not UNSCHEDULED. DUPLICATED is 6, which is present and is not 2, so every trip this sentence forbids is one E013 already reports. E013 also covers the VehiclePosition half, which S022 did not. Measured over S022's own fixture in modern mode, one message: E013 'trip_id T1 schedule_relationship DUPLICATED' beside S022 'trip_id T1 is DUPLICATED but frequencies.txt gives it exact_times=0'. Compat could not have shown this and no differential would have: the 2015 enum has no DUPLICATED, protobuf-java files the value as an unknown field, hasScheduleRelationship() answers false, and the pinned jar's verdict on that fixture is W009 alone. This clause was first recorded as overlapping nothing, on the strength of S022's own sentence, 'Nothing in the 56 reads DUPLICATED at all: it is post-2015 and the 2015 descriptor has no member for it', which is true and is not the question, because E013 never reads the member by name. S022 was retired rather than shipped with a permanent exemption from tests/test_tier_overlap.py, on the same principle as P014 at 143#2 in the practice verdicts. Restoring the module and this verdict is what reverses it.

1064#1.note: S036 enforces the scheme half whole and the escaping half in part. Checked, because the bytes decide it: a character RFC 3986 does not let a URI carry literally (a space, a control character, a non-ASCII character, one of "<>\^`{|}), and a % that does not begin a two-hex-digit escape. Not checked, and still rejected under R2: the rest, because a URL whose reserved characters were never escaped and one that needed no escaping are the same bytes. The escaping half is a must reported at WARNING, since one rule declares one severity and the scheme half is a should.
